notes: §1985:VII.4.7.4 GR18 defines the end-of-page condition (the write "causes the LINAGE-COUNTER to equal or exceed the value specified by integer-2"; the WRITE is executed, then imperative-statement-1) and the automatic page overflow (the write "would cause the LINAGE-COUNTER to exceed the value specified by integer-1"; the record is presented before or after the device is repositioned to the first line of the next logical page, then imperative-statement-1 if specified). PositionOnLogicalPage is that rule at every edition: counter + lines > page body takes BeginNextLogicalPage (rest of the body, bottom margin, next page, counter 1) and sets the condition; otherwise the counter advances and counter >= footing start sets it only when FOOTING is specified (§1985:VII.3.7.4 GR1: "If the FOOTING phrase is not specified, no end-of-page condition independent of the page overflow condition exists."). The strict '>' is the 1985 wording. WriteAdvancingRecord orders presentation and travel by BEFORE or AFTER, and WriteRecord sends a WRITE with no ADVANCING phrase through it as AFTER 1. The 1985 difference from 2023 (a WRITE without the phrase raises nothing) holds at 85: the write is successful (status 00), EmitUseHook dispatches a USE procedure on an unsuccessful status only, and no exception-condition checking can be enabled at 85. Probed at --std 85 beyond the witness: top and bottom margins in the written file (14 blank lines counted across an overflow followed by ADVANCING PAGE), ADVANCING 0 outside the footing area, an advance larger than the body, AFTER 2 with no phrase across three pages, data-name operands re-read at the page change, and USE ... ON OUTPUT not run by a footing or overflow write without the phrase.

next.reason: 1985 confines the end-of-page condition to 'a given WRITE statement with the END-OF-PAGE phrase'; a WRITE without it only repositions on automatic page overflow. §2023:14.9.51.4 GR26 raises an end-of-page condition for any WRITE to a LINAGE file whose lines 'do not fit within the current page body' (the footing case only when FOOTING is specified, §2023:13.18.34.4 GR1), and §2023:14.9.51.4 GR27 sets EC-I-O-EOP or EC-I-O-EOP-OVERFLOW and, without the phrase, transfers control to an exception-checking PERFORM WHEN or an applicable USE declarative. The overflow threshold is also restated ('equal to or exceeds the page size' against 1985 'would cause the LINAGE-COUNTER to exceed integer-1'). Different requirement.
